content_voiceover: This page has a single detailed question on targeted therapies for AML, asking which statement is wrong. The answer is the statement describing type one and type two FLT3 inhibitors, and it has the definitions reversed. In reality, type one FLT3 inhibitors bind the kinase in its active conformation and can inhibit both FLT3 internal tandem duplication and FLT3 TKD mutations, while type two inhibitors only bind the inactive conformation and therefore only inhibit FLT3 ITD, not TKD mutations, since a TKD mutation in the activation loop prevents that inactive conformation from forming. The other statements on this slide are accurate teaching points worth remembering, oral azacitidine, known as CC 486 or Onureg, prolongs overall and relapse free survival as maintenance therapy in older AML patients after achieving first remission, quizartinib, crenolanib, and gilteritinib are considered second generation FLT3 inhibitors with greater specificity and fewer off target effects, midostaurin remains the first approved drug for newly diagnosed FLT3 mutated AML, and venetoclax combined with low dose cytarabine is approved for patients over seventy five or those unfit for intensive chemotherapy.
keypoints: Type I FLT3 inhibitors block active conformation, inhibiting both ITD and TKD mutations
Type II FLT3 inhibitors only bind inactive conformation, inhibiting ITD alone
Oral azacitidine (CC-486) prolongs survival as post-remission maintenance in older AML
Venetoclax plus low-dose cytarabine suits patients over 75 or unfit for intensive chemotherapy
keypoint_voiceover: The trap on this page is the type one versus type two FLT3 inhibitor definition, type one hits both ITD and TKD, type two only hits ITD. Also remember oral azacitidine as maintenance therapy, and venetoclax with low dose cytarabine for older or unfit patients.
